facts.fact_text: At around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants positioned themselves, holding banners, in the vicinity of the State Duma at some distance from other protesters.

According to the applicants, they read on various online social networks that many people intended to stage solo pickets (одиночные пикеты) on 19 December 2012 in front of the State Duma to express their opposition to the draft law prohibiting adoption of children of Russian nationality by US citizens.

The justice of the peace found it established, on the basis of administrative records and testimony of police officers, that the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, had taken part in a picket involving fifty people on 19 December 2012.
According to the applicants, they were arrested by the police several minutes after positioning themselves near the State Duma on 19 December 2012.
According to the applicants, they were brought to a police station after their arrest on 19 December 2012.
At 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the police drew up a record of administrative escorting (протокол административного доставления) in respect of each applicant.
A record of administrative arrest (протокол административного задержания) drawn up at 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 stated that the applicants had arrived at the police station at 10.30 a.m.

At the police station both applicants were accused of organising and holding a group public event without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

The justice of the peace found that the picket on 19 December 2012 was unlawful because no notification had been submitted by the organisers as required by the Public Events Act (PEA).
Since 6 January 2013 Moscow City Law no. 10 of 4 April 2007 provides that the distance between solo demonstrations should be no less than fifty meters.

Moscow City Law no. 10 of 4 April 2007 (as applicable since 6 January 2013) specifies in section 2.3 that simultaneous demonstrations should be treated as solo demonstrations provided that they do not have a common goal and organisation.
